content: The procedures were conducted by the University of Sydney's data review team, with support from a GRADE methodologist. The guidelines were developed in compliance with the requirements of the Guideline Review Committee. These guidelines will be made available for free download on the WHO website as part of the comprehensive WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis. They will also be widely disseminated at international and regional conferences and meetings involving program managers across all regions. In addition to the guidelines, WHO will release an operational handbook containing practical details to aid in the programmatic implementation of the new or revised recommendations. National programs will receive support from WHO, as well as technical and funding partners, to develop national plans for managing drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB). Implementers are encouraged to establish a supportive policy and programmatic environment, including national and local policies and standard operating procedures, to facilitate the implementation of these recommendations. Efforts should also focus on promoting universal health coverage and providing public financing for DR-TB management. Dedicated resources should be allocated for staff development and community-based service delivery. Training for frontline healthcare staff and students in critical areas such as diagnosis, regimen design, patient support, treatment monitoring, and adverse reaction management is essential. The adoption of these WHO recommendations will be monitored through the annual data collection of the WHO Global TB Data Monitoring system. The Guideline Development Group (GDG) meetings for the 2022 update of the WHO treatment guidelines for drug-resistant TB were chaired by Holger J. Schünemann (GRADE methodologist, Cochrane Canada & McMaster University, Canada) and Jeremiah Muhwa Chakaya (technical expert, National TB Programme, Kenya). The GDG included a diverse group of experts, including clinicians, researchers, laboratory specialists, and program managers from various countries and institutions. The external review group and evidence reviewers also contributed to the guideline development process. These declarations were assessed by the WHO secretariat to identify and manage any potential conflicts of interest. In cases where significant conflicts were identified, individuals were either excluded from the GDG or asked to refrain from contributing to specific decision-making processes. The guidelines also reference previous WHO treatment guidelines for drug-resistant TB, including updates from 2011, 2016, 2018, and 2020. These updates are part of the WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis, specifically Module 4, which focuses on the treatment of drug-resistant TB. The guidelines and their annexes are accessible online for further reference.
